title: Magnetgreifer, System aus Magnetgreiferaufnahmevorrichtung und Magnetgreifern sowie Handhabungsvorrichtung

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0032) The gripper base section (housing) contains a piston (which displaces the magnet) and a magnet section with holding magnets, which act as pole shoes.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: (non-English passage at claim 5) The piston rod, which carries the magnet section, is displaceable along a longitudinal axis, moving the magnet between gripping and release positions.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0033) The reference discloses holding magnets (pole shoes) that contact the workpiece, but they are attached to a receiving body on the piston rod, not directly to the main housing (gripper base section).

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes holding magnets for gripping but does not explicitly mention pole shoes designed to guide or concentrate the magnetic field to a specific contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0033) The reference describes a plate-shaped receiving body for the magnets, which implies a contact surface generally perpendicular to the displacement axis (L), which would be 180 degrees. However, it does not explicitly state the angle or the range of 170-190 degrees.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0032) The reference discloses a magnetic gripper with a housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes (holding magnets), but it does not explicitly state that the contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to the displacement direction, although a perpendicular contact surface is implied.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0011) The reference describes a gripping state where the magnet section is in magnetic gripping connection with the workpiece, implying the workpiece is held by magnetic force against the contact surfaces.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: (non-English passage at claim 5) The piston rod's longitudinal axis (L) is the direction of displacement, and the housing (gripper base section) is implicitly aligned with this axis.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: The reference mentions holding magnets but does not describe any active structure on the pole shoes specifically for directing the magnetic field portion.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any active structure with a bevel on the pole shoes.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with multiple projections for directing the magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections with recesses between them.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.

features.note: The reference mentions multiple holding magnets but does not describe them as distinct north and south pole shoes or their magnetic polarity.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0032) The magnet is displaced pneumatically by a pressure medium acting on the piston.

claims.note: (non-English passage at claim 3) This passage discloses a magnetic gripper for gripping a magnetic workpiece.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0033) This passage describes a magnet section with holding magnets arranged on a receiving body, which is part of a piston rod that can be displaced along a longitudinal axis to grip and release a workpiece.
The reference describes a magnet section with holding magnets, but does not explicitly mention pole shoes attached to a housing that guide a magnetic field portion to a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not describe a contact surface angle between a workpiece contact surface and a displacement direction, nor does it specify a range for such an angle.
The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a magnet and a stripping section, but it does not specify any contact surface angle for pole shoes, nor does it mention pole shoes explicitly.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0008) The reference states that the gripper base section (housing) can be cylindrical, implying it extends along a longitudinal axis.

(non-English passage at claim 5) The reference explicitly states that the piston rod (which carries the magnet section) is displaceable along a longitudinal axis, which aligns with the displacement direction.
The reference describes a magnet section with holding magnets and a stripping section, but it does not mention pole shoes or an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
The reference does not mention a bevel on the active structure.
The reference does not mention a bevel or a bevel angle.
The reference does not mention a bevel angle or specific ranges for it.
The reference mentions multiple holding magnets and a friction element, but not a plurality of projections for directing the magnetic field portion and forming a workpiece contact surface.

The reference discloses multiple scrapers (41a, 41b, 41c, 41d) which could be considered projections, but it does not explicitly state that these include at least a first and a second projection in the context of the active structure and recess as defined in the claim.

The reference describes multiple scrapers (41a, 41b, 41c, 41d) arranged radially around the longitudinal axis, but it does not explicitly state that a first and second projection are adjacent to one another in the context of the claim's active structure.

The reference describes a scraper cavity (42) within a scraper (41a) or multiple scrapers, but it does not describe an 'active structure' with a 'recess between the first projection and the second projection' as specified in the claim.
The reference does not disclose any specific dimensions or relationships between the depth/length of a recess and the length of projections.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0009) The reference discloses a magnet section with multiple holding magnets for gripping a workpiece, which implies some form of positioning, but it does not explicitly mention a dedicated 'positioning device' for the workpiece on a contact surface.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0009) The reference discloses a magnet section with at least one holding magnet, and can have several individual holding magnets, but it does not explicitly refer to them as 'pole shoes' or specify a first and second pole shoe.
The reference does not disclose the arrangement of pole shoes as north and south poles in a gripping position.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0032) The reference discloses that the piston and piston rod, which carry the magnet section, are displaceable by means of a pressure medium (pneumatically).
(non-English passage at claim 19) This passage discloses a magnetic gripper having a status sensor for detecting a gripping state and a release state.
The reference discloses a sensor for detecting gripping and release states, but not specifically a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
The reference does not explicitly mention a receptacle in the housing for receiving a workpiece sensor or a supply line.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0030) This passage describes a handling device (manipulator) with a counter-mounting section for connecting to a mounting section of the gripper, which serves as a manipulator interface.
This reference does not disclose a housing portion designed to suppress the escape of the magnetic field.
This reference does not disclose a shielding device to prevent the magnetic field from escaping the housing.
This passage describes a system for a handling device that includes a magnetic gripper receiving device for receiving magnetic grippers.
(non-English passage at claim 3) This passage discloses a magnetic gripper for gripping a magnetizable and/or magnetic workpiece, but does not explicitly state it is a 'ferromagnetic' workpiece.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0011) This passage describes a gripping state where the magnet section is in magnetic gripping connection with the workpiece.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0011) This passage describes a release state where the magnetic gripping connection between the magnet section and the workpiece is released.
The reference does not disclose any specific length or thickness relationship for projections or workpieces.
The reference describes an 'Aufnahmeabschnitt' (receiving section) but not specifically a receptacle in the form of a groove.
